description.en: What FundsXML is, who uses it, and how a FundsXML document is built: control data, funds and asset master data, and the modules the schema offers beyond that.

say.en: In this video you learn what FundsXML is, and how a FundsXML document is built. It takes about three minutes.

Fund data travels a long way. Asset managers, fund administrators, custodian banks, distributors, data vendors and regulators all exchange net asset values, portfolios, costs and regulatory data. Without a common format, every pair of partners agrees on its own files, and every change costs time and money.
FundsXML is the answer: an open, free XML standard for fund data, made by the European fund industry. Its schema is published on GitHub under the MIT license, so anyone can use it.
Here is a real FundsXML document: the portfolio of an equity fund. It starts with the root element FundsXML4, and it names its schema, FundsXML4.xsd.
Fold the document to its main parts, and its structure becomes clear. There are three blocks: ControlData, Funds, and AssetMasterData.
ControlData describes the delivery itself: a unique document ID, the content date, the data supplier, and whether the data is new or a correction.
Funds holds one or more funds, each with its static data like names and identifiers, its dynamic data like the net asset value and the portfolio, and its share classes.
AssetMasterData describes every security once: a share, a bond, a fund, a derivative. The positions in the portfolio only refer to it.

Click any element, and the Properties panel shows what the schema says about it: its type, its place in the document and its documentation. The FundsXML schema documents every element, in several languages.

This file uses only a part of the standard. The schema also offers documents, the data of management companies, regulatory reporting like the European MiFID Template, the European ESG Template, PRIIPs data and the Tripartite Template, and country-specific data, for example for Austria and Germany.
Thanks for watching. In the next video, you set up FreeXmlToolkit for FundsXML. The links are on the screen and in the description below.
